evaluations.evidence: create a new game
evaluations.rationale: Creating a new game is a self-contained feature and does not inherently require another backlog story to be implemented first.

evaluations.evidence: invite estimators by giving them a URL where they can access the game
evaluations.rationale: Inviting estimators to access a game inherently requires a game to exist first (creation of a game).

evaluations.evidence: start a round by entering an item
evaluations.rationale: Starting a round to estimate an item inherently depends on a game/session having been created.

evaluations.evidence: see all items we try to estimate this session
evaluations.rationale: Seeing all items for the session requires that items exist (i.e., items must have been added/imported previously).

evaluations.evidence: select an item to be estimated or re-estimated
evaluations.rationale: Selecting an item to estimate/re-estimate inherently depends on items being present in the list (added/imported).

evaluations.evidence: add an item to the list of items to be estimated
evaluations.rationale: Adding an item is self-contained and does not require another backlog story to be implemented first.

evaluations.evidence: edit an item in the list of items to be estimated
evaluations.rationale: Editing an item presupposes that an item already exists in the list; it depends on the ability to add/import items.

evaluations.evidence: delete an item from the list of items to be estimated
evaluations.rationale: Deleting an item requires that items exist in the list (i.e., items must have been added/imported).

evaluations.evidence: show all estimates immediately
evaluations.rationale: Showing estimates immediately is a behavior of the estimation UI and does not inherently require another specific backlog story to be implemented first.

evaluations.evidence: accept the average of all estimates
evaluations.rationale: Accepting an average presupposes that a round with estimates exists (i.e., rounds/items must be started/estimated first).

evaluations.evidence: have the "estimate" field filled in automatically if all estimators show the same card
evaluations.rationale: Auto-filling an estimate when all estimators show the same card requires the round/estimation mechanism to collect and reveal estimates (a started round).

evaluations.evidence: enter the agreed-upon estimate
evaluations.rationale: Entering an agreed-upon estimate is meaningful only in the context of a round/item that has been estimated; it depends on starting rounds/items.

evaluations.evidence: estimate a story we estimated earlier in the session again
evaluations.rationale: Re-estimating a previously estimated story presupposes the ability to select a previously used item (select/re-estimate capability).

evaluations.evidence: import stories from a spreadsheet
evaluations.rationale: Importing stories from a spreadsheet is a self-contained feature and does not inherently require another backlog story first.

evaluations.evidence: copy/paste stories from a spreadsheet
evaluations.rationale: Copy/paste import is self-contained and does not inherently depend on another backlog story.

evaluations.evidence: browse through previous games
evaluations.rationale: Browsing previous games requires that games exist (i.e., game creation must be implemented).

evaluations.evidence: view a transcript of a game
evaluations.rationale: Viewing a game's transcript requires that a game and its transcript/data have been produced (game creation/play must exist).

evaluations.evidence: export a transcript of a game as a HTML file
evaluations.rationale: Exporting a game's transcript requires the transcript/viewing capability to exist first.

evaluations.evidence: export a transcript of a game as a CSV file
evaluations.rationale: Exporting a transcript presupposes that the game transcript exists and can be accessed/viewed.

evaluations.evidence: delete a game
evaluations.rationale: Deleting a game presupposes that games exist; it depends on the ability to create/store games.

evaluations.evidence: create an account for the application
evaluations.rationale: Account creation is a self-contained user/account feature that does not inherently depend on another backlog story.

evaluations.evidence: log in using my account name and password
evaluations.rationale: Logging in requires that an account exists (account creation must be implemented first).

evaluations.evidence: change my account details
evaluations.rationale: Changing account details presupposes an existing account (account creation required).

evaluations.evidence: delete my account
evaluations.rationale: Deleting an account requires that the account exists first (account creation).

evaluations.evidence: see dates and times in my local timezone
evaluations.rationale: Displaying dates/times in local timezone is a presentation feature and does not inherently require another backlog story first.

evaluations.evidence: get a password reminder by email
evaluations.rationale: Password reminder requires that an account with an email exists (account creation required).

evaluations.evidence: select whether to have the team estimate with {0, 1/2, 1, 2, 3, 5, 8, etc.} or {0, 1, 2, 4, 8, 16, 32, etc.}
evaluations.rationale: Choosing estimation card sets is a configuration feature that can be implemented independently and does not inherently depend on another specific backlog story.

evaluations.evidence: invite up to 15 estimators
evaluations.rationale: Limiting invites to 15 is inherently a constraint on the invitation feature; it depends on the invitation capability being implemented.

evaluations.evidence: join a game by entering my name on the page I received the URL for
evaluations.rationale: Joining a game via URL presupposes that a game and invitation/url mechanism exist (game creation and invite feature).

evaluations.evidence: see the item we're estimating
evaluations.rationale: Seeing the item being estimated requires that a round/item has been started and selected for estimation.

evaluations.evidence: see all items we will try to estimate this session
evaluations.rationale: Showing the session's items depends on those items having been added/imported into the session.

evaluations.evidence: immediately see that an estimate has been given by a specific estimator
evaluations.rationale: Indicating that a specific estimator has given an estimate presupposes that estimators can join and play (join functionality must exist).

evaluations.evidence: be shown all estimates at the same time after all estimators have given their estimate
evaluations.rationale: Simultaneously revealing estimates requires a started round and the ability for estimators to submit estimates (round and join functionality).

evaluations.evidence: change my estimate up until the last person selects a card and all are shown
evaluations.rationale: Changing an estimate during a draw presupposes the draw/estimation mechanism and participants who can play cards (join and reveal behavior).

evaluations.evidence: see each estimator's prior estimates for the story being estimated
evaluations.rationale: Viewing prior estimates requires stored/history access to prior rounds/estimates; it depends on the ability to scroll/view prior rounds.

evaluations.evidence: see who gave what estimates during the current round
evaluations.rationale: Showing which participant gave which estimate presupposes participant/join and estimate submission functionality.

evaluations.evidence: be able start a two-minute countdown timer that all participants can see
evaluations.rationale: Starting a shared countdown timer is a standalone feature and does not inherently require another backlog story to be implemented first.

evaluations.evidence: have the two-minute timer reset itself as soon as we all play an estimate
evaluations.rationale: Automatic reset of the timer upon all players playing an estimate depends on the timer feature and the estimation submission/tracking behavior.

evaluations.evidence: scroll back through the stories and estimates from prior rounds
evaluations.rationale: Scrolling back through prior rounds requires that prior rounds and their stored data exist (round-starting and storage).

evaluations.evidence: always have the cards in the same order across multiple draws
evaluations.rationale: Maintaining a consistent card order is a UI/UX requirement that does not inherently depend on other backlog stories.

evaluations.evidence: change my estimate as long as the draw has not been completed
evaluations.rationale: Allowing estimate changes during a draw presupposes the draw/estimate submission mechanism and participants being able to join/play.

evaluations.evidence: have a small thumbnail photo displayed near where my cards are played
evaluations.rationale: Displaying a thumbnail is a presentation feature; there is no explicit backlog story requiring account/profile creation to be implemented first, so no concrete dependency is identified.

evaluations.evidence: written a site which is compliant with XHTML and CSS standards
evaluations.rationale: Standards compliance is an implementation quality requirement and does not inherently depend on another backlog story.

evaluations.evidence: have a list of definitions for commonly used terms
evaluations.rationale: Providing definitions is self-contained documentation work and does not inherently require another backlog story to be implemented first.

evaluations.evidence: created database indexes
evaluations.rationale: Creating database indexes is a developer task independent of other specific backlog stories.

evaluations.evidence: application function correctly in Internet Explorer 6 and 7, Firefox 1.5 and 2, and Safari 2
evaluations.rationale: Cross-browser compatibility is an implementation requirement and does not inherently depend on another backlog story.

evaluations.evidence: site comply with the W3C accessibility guidelines where possible
evaluations.rationale: Accessibility compliance is an implementation quality requirement and is not inherently dependent on another specific backlog story.

evaluations.evidence: have the application respond quickly to my actions
evaluations.rationale: Performance/responsiveness is a system quality requirement and does not inherently require another backlog story first.

evaluations.evidence: be able to use Unicode
evaluations.rationale: Unicode support is a platform/implementation requirement and does not inherently depend on another backlog story.

evaluations.evidence: see sensible and predictable URLs
evaluations.rationale: Sensible URLs are a design/implementation concern and do not inherently require other backlog stories first.

evaluations.evidence: have nice error pages when something goes wrong
evaluations.rationale: Error page design is self-contained and does not inherently depend on another backlog story.

evaluations.evidence: results to be stored in a non-identifiable way
evaluations.rationale: Specifying non-identifiable storage for research results is a data-handling requirement and is not inherently dependent on another backlog story being implemented first.

evaluations.evidence: be able to see some metrics on use of the game
evaluations.rationale: Providing usage metrics requires that games/usage data exist and are recorded (game creation/play must exist to generate metric data).
